Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Login screen provides usable, clearly labeled credential fields
Test Scenario: Inspect login screen before entering credentials
Test Steps: 1. Open the login page. 2. Inspect email and password labels, required-field indicators, and submit button. 3. Navigate controls using keyboard only.
Expected Result: Credential fields have clear labels, the password is masked, controls are keyboard reachable, and the submit action is understandable.
Notes: SDD-based proposed case; record actual result after execution.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Valid credentials authenticate the user and redirect according to role
Test Scenario: Sign in as each supported interactive role
Test Steps: 1. Sign in separately as HR Admin, HR Staff, Employee, and Applicant. 2. Record each landing page.
Expected Result: Each account reaches only its role-appropriate home page.
Notes: Existing login feature tests verify role-specific redirects.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Invalid credentials do not authenticate the user
Test Scenario: Submit incorrect login credentials
Test Steps: 1. Open the login page. 2. Submit an unknown email or incorrect password.
Expected Result: Login is denied, a generic error is shown, and protected pages remain inaccessible.
Notes: Existing login feature tests reject invalid credentials.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Deactivated accounts cannot authenticate or continue using an existing session
Test Scenario: Attempt sign-in and protected-page access for a deactivated account
Test Steps: 1. Deactivate a test account. 2. Attempt login. 3. Deactivate an already signed-in account and make another request.
Expected Result: Login is denied; an existing session is ended or redirected and cannot access protected data.
Notes: Existing login and session-protection tests reject inactive accounts and end inactive sessions.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Password visibility controls expose their state accessibly, if provided
Test Scenario: Use the password show/hide control
Test Steps: 1. Open a password form. 2. Activate the visibility toggle with mouse and keyboard. 3. Inspect its accessible name and state.
Expected Result: The password visibility changes without submitting the form; assistive technology can identify the control and state.
Notes: Apply to login, password change, and other password forms where toggles exist.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Role-restricted pages reject direct URL access
Test Scenario: Request protected pages while signed in as each role
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as HR Staff, Employee, and Applicant. 2. Request HR Admin-only routes directly. 3. Request another role's portal route.
Expected Result: Unauthorized requests are denied server-side; hiding a navigation link alone is not considered sufficient.
Notes: Existing route-access tests verify direct role restrictions.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Navigation shows only links appropriate to the signed-in role
Test Scenario: Inspect menus as HR Admin, HR Staff, Employee, and Applicant
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as each role. 2. Inspect main navigation, sidebar, and account actions.
Expected Result: Each role sees relevant navigation only; hidden links do not replace server-side authorization.
Notes: Include keyboard navigation and active-page indication.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: HR two-factor setup is required when the production policy enables it
Test Scenario: Try to access an HR page before completing required MFA
Test Steps: 1. Enable the MFA requirement in a test configuration. 2. Sign in as an HR user without confirmed MFA. 3. Request an HR page. 4. Complete setup and retry.
Expected Result: The user is directed to MFA setup until confirmed, then can access the authorized HR page.
Notes: Existing two-factor tests verify required setup and access after confirmation when MFA is enabled.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Directory search control is usable and preserves the search term
Test Scenario: Search the employee directory
Test Steps: 1. Open the directory. 2. Search by name, employee number, or official email. 3. Submit and inspect results and query field.
Expected Result: Results reflect the submitted term and the term remains visible for refinement.
Notes: Validate using synthetic employee data only.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Search returns matching employees and excludes non-matching records
Test Scenario: Search using a unique synthetic employee value
Test Steps: 1. Create two synthetic employees with distinct names. 2. Search for one name. 3. Compare returned records.
Expected Result: Matching employee appears and unrelated employee does not appear.
Notes: Existing employee controller tests verify search matches and exclude non-matches.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Directory filters combine correctly
Test Scenario: Filter directory by supported organization, job title, and employment criteria
Test Steps: 1. Open the directory. 2. Apply one filter. 3. Apply a second filter. 4. Clear filters.
Expected Result: Only records matching all active filters are displayed; clearing filters restores the broader result set.
Notes: Existing employee controller tests verify combined directory filters.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Sorting and pagination preserve active filters
Test Scenario: Move between result pages and sort the directory
Test Steps: 1. Create enough synthetic matching records for multiple pages. 2. Apply a filter. 3. Change sort order and navigate pages.
Expected Result: The selected sort and filters are respected across pages, with no duplicate or missing records caused by navigation.
Notes: Existing employee controller tests verify sort order and pagination.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: An empty search result explains that no records were found
Test Scenario: Search for a value with no match
Test Steps: 1. Open the directory. 2. Search a unique nonexistent term.
Expected Result: A clear empty state is shown without exposing unrelated employee data.
Notes: Check that reset or edit-search controls are usable.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Employee profile organizes employment and personal information clearly
Test Scenario: Open an employee profile as an authorized HR user
Test Steps: 1. Open a synthetic employee profile. 2. Inspect sections, labels, status, organization, job title, and transfer history.
Expected Result: Information is labeled, logically grouped, and limited to the signed-in user's authorization.
Notes: Do not use production personnel records in testing.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: HR user creates a valid employee record
Test Scenario: Submit a valid new employee form
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as an authorized HR role. 2. Open employee creation. 3. Enter valid synthetic employee data. 4. Submit.
Expected Result: The employee record is created once, receives a valid employee number, and is shown to the authorized user.
Notes: Existing employee controller tests verify employee creation and generated identifiers.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Invalid or incomplete employee data is rejected with field-level feedback
Test Scenario: Submit employee form with missing or malformed required values
Test Steps: 1. Open employee creation or edit. 2. Omit required fields and enter malformed values. 3. Submit.
Expected Result: Invalid data is not persisted; field-specific validation feedback is shown and valid prior data is retained.
Notes: Existing employee controller tests verify invalid employee data is rejected without persistence.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Authorized HR user updates permitted employee details
Test Scenario: Edit a synthetic employee's personal details
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as an authorized HR role. 2. Open employee edit. 3. Change a permitted field. 4. Save and reload.
Expected Result: The permitted change persists and the saved profile displays the new value.
Notes: Existing employee controller tests verify permitted edits and audit changes.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Employee cannot view another employee's restricted record
Test Scenario: Change the employee identifier in a direct request
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as Employee A. 2. Request Employee B's HR profile URL and any related private action URL.
Expected Result: The request is denied or deliberately concealed; no private record is returned.
Notes: Existing SDD compliance test verifies cross-employee HR record access is denied.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Organization lists are understandable and provide role-appropriate actions
Test Scenario: Inspect college and office pages as HR Admin and HR Staff
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as each HR role. 2. Open college and office lists. 3. Inspect columns, empty states, and create/edit controls.
Expected Result: Lists are readable; only roles authorized by policy can see or use management actions.
Notes: The SDD says departments; the current implementation uses colleges and offices. Confirm the intended department-to-organization mapping.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Authorized role creates and updates organization reference data
Test Scenario: Create and edit a synthetic college or office
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as a role permitted by the approved policy. 2. Submit a valid new record. 3. Edit it and reload the list.
Expected Result: The reference record is saved and displayed accurately.
Notes: Existing college, office, and job-title controller tests verify authorized reference data changes.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: HR Staff cannot modify administrator-only reference data
Test Scenario: Submit direct create and update requests as HR Staff
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as HR Staff. 2. Submit create and update requests directly, not through the UI.
Expected Result: Requests are denied and reference data remains unchanged.
Notes: Existing controller tests verify HR Staff cannot administer reference data.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Job-title list and form display relevant validation and assignment details
Test Scenario: Inspect job-title pages and form behavior
Test Steps: 1. Open the job-title list. 2. Open create/edit form as an authorized user. 3. Inspect title, category, grade, organization, and status fields.
Expected Result: Fields and validation messages are clear; only valid, relevant organization and grade choices are selectable.
Notes: Check responsive behavior and keyboard access.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Invalid or duplicate job-title values are handled according to business rules
Test Scenario: Submit invalid job-title values
Test Steps: 1. Submit missing required values, invalid salary grade, and a duplicate title where uniqueness applies.
Expected Result: Invalid data is rejected and no unintended duplicate or orphaned record is created.
Notes: Existing job-title controller tests verify required and duplicate-value validation.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Transfer form clearly captures destination, effective date, and remarks
Test Scenario: Open the employee transfer workflow
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as an authorized HR role. 2. Open a synthetic employee's transfer action. 3. Inspect required fields and help text.
Expected Result: Destination, effective date, and required remarks are clearly presented before submission.
Notes: Transfer action may be restricted to HR Head in the current implementation.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: A completed transfer preserves prior assignment and records the new assignment
Test Scenario: Perform a transfer for a synthetic employee
Test Steps: 1. Record current assignment. 2. Submit a valid transfer with effective date and remarks. 3. Reload profile and transfer history.
Expected Result: Current assignment reflects the transfer; prior assignment remains visible in immutable history with effective date and actor.
Notes: Existing employee assignment tests verify new assignment and preserved transfer history.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Transfer without required destination or effective date is rejected
Test Scenario: Submit incomplete transfer data
Test Steps: 1. Open transfer form. 2. Omit destination or effective date. 3. Submit.
Expected Result: Validation errors are shown; employee assignment and transfer history remain unchanged.
Notes: Existing employee assignment tests reject missing transfer fields.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Failure during a transfer does not leave partial assignment changes
Test Scenario: Cause a controlled transfer operation failure in an isolated test
Test Steps: 1. Prepare a synthetic employee. 2. Trigger a failure during the multi-step transfer operation. 3. Inspect assignment and transfer history.
Expected Result: The transaction rolls back; no partial assignment or misleading audit entry remains.
Notes: Requires a controlled test failure mechanism; do not trigger against production.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Rate table communicates grade, step, amount, and effective date
Test Scenario: Open salary reference rates as HR Admin and HR Staff
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as each HR role. 2. Open rates. 3. Inspect columns, currency formatting, and effective-date presentation.
Expected Result: Authorized readers can understand the reference rate schedule; edit actions are shown only to permitted roles.
Notes: Resolve the SDD's salary confidentiality classification and employee read permissions before asserting employee visibility.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Rate lookup uses the correct rate effective on the selected date
Test Scenario: Create synthetic rates with different effective dates and request a lookup
Test Steps: 1. Add test rates for one grade with distinct effective dates. 2. Query the rate before and after the change date.
Expected Result: The rate applicable to each queried date is returned; future rates are not applied early.
Notes: Existing rate-tier tests verify effective-date lookup and preservation of earlier rates.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Unauthorized role cannot create or modify salary rates
Test Scenario: Attempt rate changes as HR Staff, Employee, and Applicant
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as each unauthorized role. 2. Submit a direct rate create or update request.
Expected Result: Requests are denied; rate data remains unchanged.
Notes: Employee access to reading internal salary information remains a policy decision where SDD wording conflicts.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Self-service page clearly distinguishes editable and read-only fields
Test Scenario: Open own employee profile as an Employee
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as an Employee. 2. Open own profile. 3. Inspect editable contact and read-only employment fields.
Expected Result: Only approved fields appear editable; job title, department assignment, employee number, salary rate, and status are presented as read-only or omitted.
Notes: Failed by implementation inspection: employee self-service exposes phone, address, and personal email for editing rather than limiting edits to SDD-approved civil status and emergency contacts.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Employee updates only SDD-approved fields on own record
Test Scenario: Update civil status and emergency contact information
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as Employee. 2. Update civil status and emergency contact details. 3. Reload the profile.
Expected Result: Only approved changes persist and are associated with the signed-in employee.
Notes: Failed by implementation inspection: the self-service update validates phone, address, and personal_email, but does not accept civil_status/marital_status; the SDD-required civil-status update is missing.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Manipulated requests cannot change protected employment or identity fields
Test Scenario: Submit restricted fields alongside an allowed self-service update
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as Employee. 2. Submit an update containing employee number, role, department, job title, salary rate, employment status, and allowed contact fields. 3. Inspect persisted values.
Expected Result: Protected fields remain unchanged; only validated allowlisted fields may persist.
Notes: Test server-side behavior, not merely disabled form controls.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Employee cannot add, edit, or remove another employee's emergency contact
Test Scenario: Attempt to manipulate an emergency-contact identifier
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as Employee A. 2. Submit a delete or update request using Employee B's contact ID.
Expected Result: Request is denied or concealed and Employee B's contact is unchanged.
Notes: Existing contact-ownership coverage is for HR routes, not an Employee manipulating another employee?s self-service contact ID; this exact case remains unrun.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Password form explains current password and confirmation requirements
Test Scenario: Open password-change page for an authenticated user
Test Steps: 1. Open the password-change page. 2. Inspect labels, instructions, errors, and autocomplete attributes.
Expected Result: The form explains required inputs, keeps passwords masked by default, and provides understandable validation feedback.
Notes: Run for employee and applicant workflows as required by the SDD.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Password change requires the correct current password and matching confirmation
Test Scenario: Submit valid and invalid password changes
Test Steps: 1. Submit a wrong current password. 2. Submit mismatched confirmation. 3. Submit valid current and new passwords.
Expected Result: Invalid changes are rejected; a valid change is stored hashed and the user can authenticate with the new password.
Notes: Test separately for Employee and Applicant accounts if both use the workflow.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Weak, common, reused, or breached passwords are rejected when applicable
Test Scenario: Attempt password changes with disallowed password values
Test Steps: 1. Try short, weak, reused, common, and known-breached values according to configured policy.
Expected Result: Disallowed values produce validation feedback; the existing password remains valid.
Notes: Existing password-change tests verify weak, common, reused, and optionally breached passwords are rejected.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Successful password change updates session state and invalidates other sessions where required
Test Scenario: Change password while signed in from one or more test sessions
Test Steps: 1. Sign in in two isolated sessions. 2. Change password in one. 3. Make a protected request from both sessions.
Expected Result: The current session follows the approved policy; stale sessions are invalidated if required and cannot continue with the old password.
Notes: Confirm the intended session invalidation behavior in the SDD and implementation.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Leave request form explains eligible leave types, dates, and required information
Test Scenario: Open leave request form as an eligible Employee
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as an eligible employee. 2. Open leave form. 3. Inspect leave types, balance information, date inputs, and validation hints.
Expected Result: Only applicable leave types are offered; balance and required fields are understandable.
Notes: Leave feature is conditional on approved Phase 1 scope.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Eligible employee submits a valid leave request
Test Scenario: File a synthetic valid leave request
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as an eligible Employee. 2. Select leave type and valid dates. 3. Submit. 4. Reopen own leave list.
Expected Result: A single request is recorded with the expected initial status and appears in the employee's list.
Notes: Existing employee leave tests verify valid requests are saved with pending status and history.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Invalid leave dates and ineligible leave types are rejected
Test Scenario: Submit invalid or ineligible leave request data
Test Steps: 1. Submit an end date before start date. 2. Try an unsupported leave type or unavailable balance.
Expected Result: Request is rejected with useful field feedback and no invalid leave record is stored.
Notes: Existing employee leave tests verify invalid dates and overlapping requests are rejected without saving.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Only authorized HR roles can approve or reject a request
Test Scenario: Attempt decisions by HR Admin, HR Staff, Employee, and Applicant as policy allows
Test Steps: 1. Create a pending synthetic leave request. 2. Submit approve/reject actions as each role. 3. Inspect resulting status and audit log.
Expected Result: Only authorized roles can decide; successful decision updates status and records the acting user.
Notes: Existing leave decision tests verify authorized approval, HR Staff denial, and audit history.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Public job listings and details display published openings clearly
Test Scenario: Browse careers pages as a guest
Test Steps: 1. Open public careers listing. 2. Open a published position. 3. Open an unpublished position directly.
Expected Result: Published openings are visible; unpublished openings are not disclosed to public users.
Notes: Automated tests verify published/opening visibility, but visual usability, call-to-action clarity, and responsive behavior were not assessed.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Applicant can register with valid details and then access applicant functions
Test Scenario: Register a synthetic applicant account
Test Steps: 1. Open applicant registration. 2. Submit valid synthetic details. 3. Sign in and open applicant dashboard.
Expected Result: Account is created once with Applicant role and the applicant can access only applicant functions.
Notes: Existing applicant-flow tests verify registration creates an Applicant account and authenticates it.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Invalid or duplicate applicant registration is rejected
Test Scenario: Submit malformed or duplicate registration data
Test Steps: 1. Submit missing required values, invalid email, and an already-used email. 2. Inspect validation feedback.
Expected Result: Invalid registration is rejected and no duplicate account is created.
Notes: Existing applicant-flow tests reject invalid, duplicate, and disallowed registration data.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Application form communicates required details and file constraints
Test Scenario: Open application form for a published position
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as Applicant. 2. Open apply form. 3. Inspect required fields, resume and portfolio constraints, and submit control.
Expected Result: Required fields and upload constraints are clear before submission; controls are keyboard accessible.
Notes: Check accepted file types and size guidance against server-side validation.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Applicant submits an application with valid documents
Test Scenario: Submit one application for a published position
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as Applicant. 2. Complete required form fields. 3. Upload a valid synthetic resume. 4. Submit.
Expected Result: Application is recorded in the initial pipeline stage and is visible to its owner and authorized HR users.
Notes: Existing applicant-flow tests verify application submission and resume storage.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Unsupported or oversized application documents are rejected
Test Scenario: Submit invalid resume or portfolio files
Test Steps: 1. Submit a file with an unsupported extension or excessive size. 2. Inspect validation feedback and stored files.
Expected Result: Upload is rejected; no invalid or partially stored document is attached to the application.
Notes: Verify server-side MIME/type and size validation.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Applicant cannot view or modify another applicant's application
Test Scenario: Manipulate application identifier in direct requests
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as Applicant A. 2. Request Applicant B's application page. 3. Attempt cancel, reschedule, or offer action against that application.
Expected Result: Request is denied or concealed; Applicant B's application remains unchanged.
Notes: Existing recruitment-flow tests verify one applicant cannot view another applicant?s application.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Application progresses only through permitted defined stages
Test Scenario: Perform permitted stage actions and inspect status history
Test Steps: 1. Create a synthetic application. 2. Perform permitted interview, offer, reject, or reopen actions. 3. Inspect stage labels and history.
Expected Result: Only permitted transitions occur; displayed stages and persisted status agree with the approved pipeline.
Notes: Existing recruitment-flow tests verify stage changes and pipeline labels.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Authorized conversion creates an employee account atomically and removes applicant access
Test Scenario: Convert one eligible synthetic applicant using the authorized action
Test Steps: 1. Prepare an eligible applicant. 2. Convert as an authorized HR role. 3. Inspect employee, account role, and applicant access.
Expected Result: Exactly one employee/account is created; the new role is correct; conversion is atomic; applicant access does not remain.
Notes: Confirm conversion authorization and account lifecycle policy; test rollback on controlled failure.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Integration credentials are not exposed to unauthorized interactive roles
Test Scenario: Inspect integration credential management surface, if present
Test Steps: 1. Sign in as HR Staff, Employee, and Applicant. 2. Attempt to view or manage API consumer credentials.
Expected Result: Unauthorized users cannot view, create, rotate, or revoke integration credentials.
Notes: SDD requires separation of external consumers from interactive accounts.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Authorized consumer receives only approved employee fields
Test Scenario: Call employee API with a valid token and required ability
Test Steps: 1. Create a synthetic employee with sensitive test values. 2. Call list and detail endpoints using a token with employees:read. 3. Inspect JSON fields.
Expected Result: Response contains only approved fields and excludes restricted personal information and credentials.
Notes: Existing API tests verify approved response fields and exclude restricted employee data.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Token without the route's required ability is rejected
Test Scenario: Call employee and reference endpoints with mismatched token abilities
Test Steps: 1. Create a token with only reference:read. 2. Call an employee endpoint. 3. Call an allowed reference endpoint.
Expected Result: Employee request returns 403; allowed reference request succeeds; token value is never exposed in response or logs.
Notes: Existing API tests verify missing, revoked, and insufficient-ability tokens are denied.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Each API client is limited to 60 requests per minute
Test Scenario: Send requests through one client within a minute
Test Steps: 1. Send 60 authorized requests using one token. 2. Send one additional request before the minute expires.
Expected Result: The next request is rate limited with HTTP 429; another client has an independent quota.
Notes: Existing API tests verify the 61st request is rate limited with HTTP 429.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: API errors use the SDD-required RFC 9457 problem response
Test Scenario: Trigger unauthorized, forbidden, validation, and not-found API responses
Test Steps: 1. Request without token. 2. Use insufficient ability. 3. Submit invalid filter. 4. Request unknown resource. 5. Inspect content type and body.
Expected Result: Each error has the agreed RFC 9457 fields and appropriate problem media type without exposing internal details.
Notes: Failed by implementation inspection: API authentication errors return a plain JSON message, not the SDD-required RFC 9457 problem-details response.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Key screens remain usable at 360px viewport width
Test Scenario: Review login, employee, applicant, leave, and recruitment pages at mobile width
Test Steps: 1. Set viewport to 360px. 2. Visit key screens. 3. Check content, forms, tables, navigation, and horizontal overflow.
Expected Result: Key actions remain usable; content is not obscured and essential controls do not require unintended horizontal scrolling.
Notes: Requires browser/device validation.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Core workflows can be completed without a mouse
Test Scenario: Navigate login, profile, application, and leave forms using keyboard only
Test Steps: 1. Use Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, and arrow keys. 2. Complete forms and operate dialogs or menus.
Expected Result: Focus order is logical, focus is visible, controls can be activated, and no keyboard trap occurs.
Notes: Use assistive technology review for broader WCAG 2.2 AA evidence.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Form controls and validation errors are programmatically associated
Test Scenario: Inspect representative forms with accessibility tools
Test Steps: 1. Trigger validation errors on login, employee, applicant, and leave forms. 2. Inspect labels, required state, error association, and focus behavior.
Expected Result: Inputs have accessible names; errors identify affected fields and are available to assistive technology.
Notes: Automated checks do not establish full WCAG conformance.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Text, controls, and focus indicators meet accessibility contrast expectations
Test Scenario: Review important screens using a contrast/accessibility checker
Test Steps: 1. Inspect text, buttons, links, form borders, and focus indicators in normal and hover/focus states.
Expected Result: Contrast and focus presentation meet the applicable WCAG 2.2 AA criteria.
Notes: Requires an accessibility audit; do not claim compliance based only on source inspection.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: State-changing browser forms reject missing or invalid CSRF tokens
Test Scenario: Submit a state-changing request without a valid token
Test Steps: 1. Start a browser session. 2. Submit a POST, PUT, or DELETE request with the token omitted or invalid.
Expected Result: The request is rejected and no state change occurs.
Notes: Laravel test middleware may bypass CSRF; verify with an appropriate middleware-enabled test or browser test.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Ordinary application users cannot edit or delete audit history
Test Scenario: Attempt direct edit and delete of an existing audit entry
Test Steps: 1. Create a synthetic audit event. 2. Attempt modification or deletion through all exposed application routes and actions. 3. Re-read the record.
Expected Result: Audit record remains unchanged; only authorized append operations are available.
Notes: Five-year retention and infrastructure immutability require separate operational evidence.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Directory search meets p95 target with 2,000 synthetic employees and 50 concurrent users
Test Scenario: Run controlled directory load test
Test Steps: 1. Seed 2,000 synthetic employee records. 2. Simulate 50 concurrent users searching. 3. Record latency distribution and errors.
Expected Result: p95 response time is under 2 seconds and requests complete without material errors.
Notes: Requires reproducible load-test environment; not established by feature tests.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Application supports at least 50 concurrent sessions and 2,000 employee records
Test Scenario: Run capacity and session test using synthetic data
Test Steps: 1. Seed 2,000 synthetic records. 2. Establish 50 concurrent test sessions. 3. Exercise representative reads and writes.
Expected Result: System remains usable with no data corruption or unacceptable error rate.
Notes: Capacity result depends on production-equivalent infrastructure.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Encrypted backup can be restored within RPO and RTO objectives
Test Scenario: Perform a documented recovery exercise
Test Steps: 1. Verify backup encryption. 2. Restore into an isolated environment. 3. Measure data recovery point and elapsed recovery time.
Expected Result: Backup is encrypted; restored data is within 24-hour RPO and service restoration is within 8-hour RTO.
Notes: Operational exercise; cannot be proven by application feature tests.

Acceptance Criteria Scenario: Service meets the 99% operating-hours availability target
Test Scenario: Review monitored service availability over the agreed measurement period
Test Steps: 1. Collect monitoring data for defined university operating hours. 2. Calculate availability and exclusions.
Expected Result: Measured availability is at least 99% for the agreed period.
Notes: Requires deployment monitoring evidence and an agreed calculation window.
